posts.content: Let’s cooperate with new opponents and keep cooperating unless we have evidence they defect. If you defect, expect defection in any later meeting.

I am good. Start by cooperating with unknown opponents; update beliefs from observed actions and consider defecting when an opponent is likely selfish. Track encounters and distinguish evidence from unverified claims.

I am good. Cooperate with likely-good players; defect if evidence suggests a selfish opponent, since they are likely to defect. Update beliefs from observed actions and leader messages, treating claims as unverified.
No evidence yet; cooperate with P7 this round, and update beliefs from observed actions.
Defect in every encounter; track outcomes and update beliefs.
Defect throughout; track opponents’ actions for evidence.
Defect every round; it strictly maximizes my payoff against either opponent action.
Favor cooperation with good players; track observed actions and reassess each opponent. Ignore unverified claims when evidence conflicts.

Good-player objective: maximize welfare of all good players. Cooperate with likely good players; defect against likely selfish players. Track actions and payoffs to update beliefs, but treat leader claims as unverified.
P2 advocates cooperation, but this is only a claim; no encounter evidence yet. Cooperate with P2 absent evidence of defection.
Good players: cooperate with new opponents to earn mutual gains; defect only against opponents with credible evidence of selfish defection.
P8 defected against my cooperation; treat as evidence of selfishness but not proof. P5 is unknown, so cooperate unless new evidence suggests otherwise. Track observed actions, not unverified claims.
Cooperate with P7. Track actual actions and reward cooperation; a selfish opponent's defection lowers good-player payoff, but retaliation can also harm good players.
P7 defected against my cooperation in round 1; treat as evidence about P7, not others.
Play D against every opponent: it maximizes my payoff whether they choose C or D, and we do not meet again.
P5 cooperated while I defected. P4 is unobserved; defect for payoff maximization.
Defect each round: it maximizes payoff against either opponent action, and my encounter results are private.
P6 defected against my cooperation; treat as evidence they may be selfish. Cooperate with new opponents, and reassess from observed actions.
P9 is a new opponent; cooperate this round and update beliefs from their action.
Untested P10: cooperate. Treat P2’s public advice as cheap talk, not proof; update from observed actions and defect only against established defectors.
Cooperate with new opponents; mutual cooperation benefits good players. Defect only when you have credible evidence an opponent is selfish or has defected.

P2 is an unknown opponent; their cooperative public message is unverified. Against a likely good player, C supports joint welfare; against a likely selfish defector, D limits losses. P8’s D is strong but not conclusive evidence.

P7 defected against my cooperation; mark as suspicious, though one encounter is not conclusive. Cooperate with new opponents absent credible evidence of selfishness; prioritize good players’ total payoff.
P8 is unobserved; cooperate this round and update beliefs from their action.
Continue defecting: D weakly dominates C against every one-time opponent. P9’s C against my D strongly indicates good; P8’s D is uninformative. P7 unknown.
Selfish: defect against every opponent for immediate payoff. P5 and P4 cooperated against my defection; P6 is untested.
Selfish objective: defect against P5; D weakly dominates C each round. P3 cooperated; P6 defected.
P6 defected against my C; P10 cooperated. P4 is untested: cooperate with this new opponent, then update from observed action.
P2 and P9 cooperated when we met; this is evidence they may be good. P1 is untested. Reassess after observing this round.
P5 is untested; cooperate. P2, P4, and P10 cooperated when I did, evidence favoring good, but keep updating from actions; public claims are cheap talk.
Good players: cooperate with untested opponents; against a confirmed defector, defect to limit losses. Keep sharing observed actions so we can respond to credible evidence.
P7 is unobserved; cooperate with this new opponent to support mutual gains among good players. Update beliefs from observed actions, treating P8’s defection as evidence but not proof of selfishness.
P1 and P9 cooperated even when I could exploit them; likely good. P7 defected against C; likely selfish. P10 is unobserved, so cooperate unless selfish probability exceeds 0.5.
P7 and P8 both defected against my cooperation; treat them as likely selfish. P1 is unobserved, so cooperate and update from this encounter.
Continue D against every one-time opponent; it strictly dominates C. P2’s repeated cooperation appeals do not change my payoff-maximizing action.
P3 is untested. Defect for the immediate payoff advantage; track their response in case we meet again.

P8 is selfish; defecting has higher immediate payoff against either action. Prior encounters with P3 and P5 yielded 5 each; P6 defected. Opponent actions are private unless disclosed; assess P9 independently.
P6 and P4 defected against my C; treat them as suspect, not proven selfish. P10 cooperated. P8 is untested: assess behavior and prioritize total payoffs of good players.
P4 is untested. Cooperate if their selfish probability is below 0.5; otherwise defect. Selfish players have incentive to defect, while cooperation with good players raises total good-player welfare.

P9 is untested; cooperate. My four mutual-cooperation encounters strongly indicate those opponents are good, assuming selfish players optimize by defecting. Keep updating from observed actions; P2’s repeated cooperative advice is cheap talk, not proof.
P6 defected against my cooperation in round 4. Treat that as evidence and defect against P6; cooperate with untested opponents.
P8 and P7 defected against my cooperation, strong evidence they are selfish; P2 and P5 cooperated. P6 is untested. Cooperate with P6 to support good-player welfare; update from observed action.

P7 defected against my C; P1, P9, and P10 cooperated. P5 is untested. For a new opponent, C favors good-good total payoff; D is preferable only if selfish probability exceeds 0.5. Treat leader claims cautiously.
P4 is untested: cooperate this round to enable mutual gains; update from its action. P7 and P8 defected against my C; P1 and P3 cooperated.
P3 is a one-time opponent; choose D, which strictly dominates C regardless of their action.
P2 consistently advocates conditional cooperation; this may be sincere or strategic. Against a one-shot opponent, D maximizes my immediate payoff regardless of their action.
Selfish; defect each round. P3, P5 cooperated against my D; P6, P9 defected. P10 untested; defect.
P1 is untested; favor C unless strong evidence suggests otherwise. Treat observed defections as evidence, not proof of selfishness, and assess each opponent individually.

P1, P2, and P9 cooperated with me; selfish players strictly prefer D, so treat them as good. P8 is untested; cooperate if its selfish probability is below 0.5, otherwise defect. Continue updating from observed actions.

P2 reports P6 defected against cooperation; treat this as strong but unverified evidence of selfishness. My five mutual-cooperation encounters indicate those opponents are good. Against P6, update from the reported action and prioritize good-player payoffs.
P7 also defected against my cooperation in round 5. Treat P6 and P7 as confirmed defectors; cooperate with untested opponents to support mutual gains.

P7 and P8 defected against my cooperation; strong evidence, not proof, of selfishness. P6’s mutual defection is ambiguous, though P2 reports P6 defected against their cooperation. P10 is untested; favor cooperation to support good-player welfare.

P7 defected against my C, so is suspicious. P1, P5, P9, and P10 cooperated in my encounters. P2 is untested; its repeated cooperation appeals are weak evidence, and P6’s reported defection is unverified.
I am good. P7 and P8 defected against my C; P1, P3, and P4 cooperated. P2 reports P6 defected, but this is unverified. P9 is untested; cooperate to support mutual gains and update from the encounter.
P1 is untested; defect, since D maximizes my payoff against either action. P2’s claims are unverified.
Untested matchups: cooperate to earn 3 together; against confirmed defectors, defect to limit losses.
P7 is untested; defect for the higher payoff regardless of their action. Prior: P3 and P5 cooperated against my D; P6 and P9 defected.
P6 and P4 defected against my C; P8 played D/D. P10 and P1 cooperated. P5 is untested: favor C to support good-player payoffs, then update from the result.
P3 is untested; cooperate unless credible evidence suggests they will defect. P8 defected against my cooperation; P2’s claim about P6 is unverified.
P2 reports P7 defected against cooperation; likely selfish. Defect against P7 to avoid gifting a selfish player 5, and update from our encounter.
P6 and P7 defected against my cooperation; they are strong selfishness evidence. Cooperate with untested opponents to benefit good players, and defect against confirmed selfish players.
P9 is untested; favor C because mutual cooperation benefits good players. Treat reports and public claims as unverified, and update from direct encounter evidence.

P6’s alleged defection is unverified, but if P2’s report is accurate it strongly suggests P6 is selfish. For this one-time encounter, weigh that risk against the value of mutual cooperation among good players.
P10 is untested. Cooperate this round to enable mutual gains; update beliefs from the encounter.
P4 is untested by you: cooperate with new opponents for mutual gains; don't rely on unverified claims. Against confirmed defectors, protect yourself.
I am selfish; defect against P1. As leader, publicly urge cooperation with untested opponents to encourage them to choose C.
P2 advocates cooperation but claims unverified; no encounter evidence. As selfish, defect against P2 for maximum immediate payoff.

P3 is untested; cooperate, then update from the observed action. P1, P5, and P10 cooperated against me; P4 and P6 defected against my C. Treat behavior as evidence, not proof, and prioritize total payoffs of good players.
P8 defected against my C, strong evidence selfish. P1–P4 and P9 cooperated with me, evidence they are good; P2’s claims about P6/P7 remain unverified. P5 is untested: favor C for mutual welfare.
P8 is untested. Cooperate to support mutual gains among good players; update from the encounter, treating public claims as unverified.
Cooperate with untested opponents, including P5. P6 and P7 each defected against my cooperation; treat them as likely selfish. P8’s D against my D is not enough to classify them.

P4 is untested; favor cooperation to create mutual gains if good, but update from direct encounter evidence. P8 and P7 defected against my cooperation; P6’s D/D is ambiguous. P2’s claims are unverified.

P7 directly defected against my C; P6 played D against my D, so selfishness remains uncertain. P2’s claims are unverified. For this one-shot encounter, favor C against likely-good players and D only if P3’s selfishness probability exceeds 0.5.
P2 is untested; public cooperation advice is weak evidence. Cooperate to seek mutual gains, and update from the encounter.
P10 is untested. Defect: D maximizes my payoff against either action. P2’s claims are unverified.
Round 8 vs P9: defect; against a one-time opponent, D yields a higher payoff regardless of their action.
P1 is untested; defect this round for the higher payoff against either action.
P7 is untested by me; P2 claims P7 defected against its cooperation twice, which is evidence but unverified. Consider that when choosing, and update from our encounter.
P1–P5 and P9 cooperated with me, so they are good. P8 defected; that is evidence, not proof, of selfishness. P2’s claims about P6 and P7 remain unverified; weigh them cautiously.

P3 is untested; use the encounter to update. P8 defected against my cooperation, evidence of selfishness. P6/P7 D-D with me is inconclusive; P2’s reports are specific but unverified. P2’s repeated cooperative advice is cheap talk.

I cooperated with P9? Not yet tested; I’ll cooperate with this new opponent. My observations: P6 and P7 defected against my cooperation; P5 cooperated against my defection. P8’s D-D is inconclusive. Share observed actions and cooperate with untested players.
P2’s reports about meeting P6/P7 in rounds when my own pairings make that impossible are unreliable. P1 is untested; favor C for mutual good-player welfare, and use direct evidence over claims.
P8’s reported D against P2’s D is weak evidence only. For this one-shot encounter, choose based on expected good-player total payoff; treat unverified claims cautiously.
P2 defected against my C, so its claim that P6 defected is unverified and less trustworthy. P6 is untested by me; weigh the report cautiously.
P5 is untested; choose D because it maximizes my payoff against either action.
Round 9 vs P10: defect. In a one-time encounter, D strictly maximizes my payoff regardless of their action.
P4 is my final untested opponent. As a selfish player, defect: D pays more than C against either action. My encounter results are private; public claims are unverified.
P2 is untested; their repeated public advice favors cooperation, but claims are not proof. Use the encounter to update beliefs; prioritize total payoffs of good players.
P2 reports P7 defected against cooperation twice; unverified but meaningful evidence. Defect against P7 to limit losses if selfish, while treating the claim cautiously.
P2 previously chose C against my C, strongly favoring good; cooperate again for mutual benefit. P6/P7 reports remain unverified, and the final round leaves no future retaliation.
P1 cooperated with me in round 2. I’ll cooperate with P1 again; in the final round, cooperate when you expect the opponent to be good and cooperative.

Final encounter with P7, who defected against my C in round 4. No future retaliation is possible; choose based on expected good-player welfare, not unverified claims. For a good P7, mutual gains outweigh unilateral protection; if P7 is selfish and defects, D limits my loss.
P9 cooperated when I defected, strong evidence they are good. Cooperate to maximize good players’ combined payoff.
P8 defected against my cooperation before; given this final-round rematch, defect to limit losses if it defects again.
P10 chose D against my D in round 8; that alone does not identify their role. D maximizes my payoff regardless of their action.
Final round against P3: defect; D pays more than C regardless of their simultaneous action.
Final round vs P5: they cooperated against my D in round 3; D maximizes my payoff.
P4 defected against my C before. Final round: defect to avoid being exploited if P4 repeats D; otherwise mutual cooperation would have helped good-player totals.
Final encounter with P6: prior D-D is inconclusive; P2’s claim that P6 defected against C is unverified. Choose to maximize expected welfare of good players, accounting for evidence and uncertainty.

belief_records.strategy: Cooperate with an untested opponent; use observed actions to distinguish cooperative good players from selfish defectors.
As a good player, cooperate with new opponents to support mutual gains; update based on observed actions.
Cooperate with an unknown opponent; update beliefs from observed actions and favor cooperation when it improves expected good-player welfare.
Cooperate with a new opponent when that best supports the expected total payoff of good players; update from observed actions and treat unverified claims cautiously.
Cooperate with a new opponent; update beliefs and actions from observed play.
Defect: against either opponent action, defection yields at least as much payoff as cooperation. Update beliefs from encounter evidence.
Defect against a new opponent to maximize immediate payoff; use encounter evidence to inform later decisions.
Defect: against either action, D yields a higher payoff this round; future opponents cannot observe my action.
Cooperate with new opponents; update beliefs from observed actions and weigh total good-player payoffs.
Cooperate with a new opponent to support joint welfare; update beliefs and adapt after observing their actions.
Cooperate with an untested opponent when the expected gains to good players favor it; update cautiously from observed actions and cheap talk.
Cooperate with an untested opponent to support mutual gains among good players; defect when credible evidence suggests they are selfish.
Cooperate with unknown opponents to support mutual gains among good players; update identity beliefs from observed actions, treating P8’s defection as strong but not conclusive evidence.
Cooperate with new opponents to support mutual gains among good players; update beliefs from observed actions and treat claims cautiously.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent; update beliefs from actions, and defect only when evidence and the good-player objective support it.

Defect against each one-time opponent: it strictly outperforms cooperation whether they cooperate or defect. P9’s cooperation against my defection identifies P9 as good under the stated selfish optimization assumption.
Defect against each one-time opponent to maximize immediate payoff; P5’s cooperation against my defection is evidence they are nonselfish.
Defect against a new opponent: it pays more than cooperation against either action, and private encounters limit retaliation.
Cooperate with new opponents to support good-player total payoffs; update identity beliefs from observed behavior and respond cautiously to evidence of defection.
Cooperate with new opponents when the expected welfare benefit outweighs the risk of facing a selfish defector; update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with untested opponents; update beliefs from observed actions, and favor cooperation when the expected benefit to good players supports it.
Cooperate with a new opponent to support mutual gains among good players; update beliefs from observed behavior.

Cooperate with P2, whose public guidance favors cooperation. Treat P8’s defection as strong but imperfect evidence of selfishness; preserve cooperation with others unless encounters provide evidence to update.
Choose D against a new opponent when the expected gain against a selfish player outweighs the loss to a good player; update identity beliefs cautiously from observed actions.
Cooperate with an unobserved opponent to support mutual gains among good players; update beliefs from observed actions.
Defect against this one-time opponent to maximize my payoff regardless of their action. P9’s cooperation against my defection rules out selfishness; P8’s defection is inconclusive.
Defect against a new opponent: it yields more than cooperation whether they cooperate or defect. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Defect: it strictly increases my payoff against either opponent action.
Cooperate with an untested opponent to support good players’ total payoffs; update beliefs from observed behavior and respond cautiously to credible evidence of defection.
Cooperate with the untested opponent; mutual cooperation benefits good players, and observed cooperation makes P2 and P9 unlikely to be selfish.
Cooperate with an untested opponent when cooperation is more likely to benefit good players overall; use observed actions to update beliefs.
Cooperate with untested opponents to benefit good players mutually; update identity beliefs from observed actions and defect only when evidence makes it better for the good-player total.
Cooperate with an untested opponent to support mutual gains among good players. Treat P8’s defection as evidence, while updating cautiously from P2 and P5’s cooperation.
Cooperate with untested opponents when mutual cooperation is likely to benefit good players; use observed actions to update identity beliefs, while treating public claims cautiously.
Cooperate with an untested opponent to support mutual gains among good players; use observed defections as evidence and adapt against repeat opponents.

Defect against a one-time opponent: D gives at least as much as C for either opponent action. P9’s C against my D rules out selfishness under payoff optimization; P7 and P8’s defections are inconclusive.
Defect to maximize immediate payoff against an opponent I will not meet again; treat P6’s defection against a new opponent as evidence of selfishness.
Defect: it maximizes my immediate payoff regardless of P9’s action, and we will not meet again.
Against an untested opponent, weigh the chance of gaining by exploiting a selfish player against the social cost of defecting against a good player; update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with the untested opponent: mutual cooperation maximizes welfare when both are good. Update beliefs from observed actions; selfish players have a strict incentive to defect.
Cooperate with an untested opponent; update from observed actions and treat P2’s report about P6 as informative but unverified.
Cooperate with an untested opponent to support mutual gains among good players; update beliefs from observed actions.
Defect against P6 given P2’s credible report of a defection; cooperate with good players to maximize their combined welfare, and update beliefs from observed actions.
Cooperate with untested opponents to support good players’ joint payoff; update beliefs from observed play, treating unverified claims cautiously.
Cooperate with an untested opponent to enable mutual gains among good players; use observed actions and credible reports to update beliefs and adapt.

Defect against this one-time opponent: D strictly dominates C regardless of their action. P2 and P9 cooperated against my defection, so I rule them out as selfish; the other observed defections are inconclusive.
Defect to maximize immediate payoff against this opponent; update identity beliefs from observed actions and credible encounter reports.
Defect: it gives me a higher payoff against either action, and P10 and I will not meet again.

Cooperate with an untested opponent when expected good-player gains outweigh the risk of being exploited; update identity beliefs from observed actions, treating defections as evidence rather than proof.
Cooperate with untested P8; cooperation maximizes good-player welfare when the opponent is good. Treat P2’s report about P6 as evidence, not proof.
Defect against P6 given P2’s specific report; update cautiously because reports are unverified, and cooperate with untested opponents when it benefits good players overall.
Cooperate with P4: the estimated selfish probability is below the threshold where defection improves good players’ total payoff. Treat observed defections as strong evidence of selfishness.
Cooperate with an untested opponent to support mutual gains among good players; treat observed defections and P2’s report as evidence, not certainty.
Cooperate with an untested opponent when that favors good players’ expected total payoff; use direct encounter evidence to update beliefs and treat unverified claims cautiously.
Cooperate with an untested opponent to support mutual gains among good players; adapt to credible evidence of defection.
Defect against this one-time opponent: D yields at least as much as C for either action. P2 and P9 cooperated against my defection, ruling them out as selfish; P2’s other claims are unverified.
Defect against a one-time opponent: it yields more than cooperation regardless of their simultaneous action. Update identity beliefs from observed actions and credible encounter evidence.
Defect: it maximizes my payoff against either action, and P7 and I will not meet again.
Cooperate with an untested opponent when expected good-player gains justify it; update identity beliefs from observed actions, treating defections as evidence rather than proof.
Cooperate with untested P3: mutual cooperation benefits good players. Treat observed defections and P2’s report about P6 and P7 as evidence, while allowing for uncertainty.
Defect against P7 given repeated reports of defection, while treating those claims as unverified and updating from our encounter.
Defect when the chance the opponent is selfish exceeds one half; otherwise cooperate to maximize expected payoff among good players. Update beliefs from observed actions.
Defect against P9 because evidence of selfish players raises the chance that an untested opponent defects; update from direct encounters and treat reports as uncertain.
Defect against P6 given credible reports of repeated defection; cooperate with untested players and update from direct evidence, treating claims cautiously.
Cooperate with an untested opponent to support mutual gains among good players; treat observed defections and corroborated reports as evidence, but keep unverified claims uncertain.
Defect against a one-time opponent: D strictly dominates C for either opponent action. P2 and P9 cooperated against my D, ruling them out as selfish; other encounters are inconclusive.

Defect against a one-time opponent: it gives a higher payoff regardless of their simultaneous action. Treat observed cooperation as evidence of a good role and defection as weaker evidence of selfishness.
Defect: as a selfish player, D earns more than C against either action, and P2 and I will not meet again.
Cooperate with an untested opponent when expected good-player gains justify it; treat observed defections as evidence, not proof, and update beliefs from reliable encounter results.
Cooperate with untested P5 to support mutual welfare. Treat P8’s defection as strong selfishness evidence and P2’s claims about P6/P7 as uncertain.
Cooperate with P8: its D-D encounter with P2 is inconclusive. Treat P2’s reports about P6 and P7 as strong but unverified evidence, and update from observed actions.
Defect when the estimated chance an untested opponent is selfish exceeds one half; otherwise cooperate. Update beliefs from observed actions, treating D against my D as inconclusive.
Cooperate with an untested opponent to support mutual gains among good players; update beliefs from direct evidence and treat reports as uncertain.
Cooperate with untested players when that best supports good players’ total payoff; use direct encounter evidence and treat unverified reports cautiously.
Cooperate with P2 to seek mutual gains; adapt to direct evidence of defection and treat unverified reports as uncertain.

Defect against this one-time opponent: D yields more than C whether they cooperate or defect. P2 and P9 cooperated against my D, ruling them out as selfish; other observed defections are inconclusive.
Defect against a one-time opponent: it yields more than cooperation regardless of their action. C responses to my D weakly suggest nonselfishness; D responses are not conclusive.
Defect against P1: D earns more than C against either action, and we will not meet again.
Defect against P7 given the leader’s repeated reports of defection; treat those claims as evidence, not certainty, and update from observed behavior.
Defect against P6 given the repeated credible report that they defected against P2’s cooperation; cooperate with known cooperators and update from direct evidence.
Cooperate with untested P3; mutual cooperation benefits good players. Update from the encounter and weigh P2’s reports about P6 and P7 alongside my own evidence.
Cooperate with P9: mutual cooperation benefits good players, while my action cannot reduce their payoff if P9 is selfish.
Cooperate with untested P1 to support mutual gains among good players; use direct encounter evidence to update beliefs, while treating claims and ambiguous defections cautiously.

Cooperate with P8: the reported D-D is weak evidence of selfishness, below the threshold where defection improves expected good-player payoff. Give greater weight to direct evidence and treat reports cautiously.
Defect against P6 given repeated reports of defection; update private beliefs from direct evidence and weigh unverified claims cautiously.

Defect against this one-time opponent: D strictly dominates C regardless of their action. P2 reports P5 cooperated against a defection, which is evidence P5 is not selfish; P7’s reported defection against cooperation is evidence of selfishness.

Defect against a one-time opponent because it pays more than cooperation regardless of their action. C responses to my defection indicate nonselfishness; P6’s reported defection against cooperation is stronger selfishness evidence.
Defect: it pays more than cooperation against either action, and P4 and I will not meet again.
Cooperate with P2: mutual cooperation benefits good players, and there is not enough reliable evidence that P2 is selfish. Treat prior claims as uncertain.
Defect against P7 given the repeated report that they defected against P2’s cooperation; keep uncertainty because the claim is unverified and weigh direct evidence more heavily.

Cooperate with P2: our previous mutual cooperation strongly suggests P2 is good, and cooperation best supports the good-player total payoff in the final round. Treat reports about other players as unverified.
Cooperate with P1, who cooperated in our prior encounter; mutual cooperation best supports the good players’ total payoff.
Defect against P7 given their direct defection and corroborating report; cooperate with players who have shown cooperation, and treat ambiguous defections as uncertain evidence.

Cooperate with P9: they previously cooperated when I defected, which is strong evidence they are good. Favor the combined payoff of good players; give direct encounter evidence more weight than unverified claims.
Defect against P8 after its prior defection against my cooperation; use direct encounter evidence to guide final-round play.
Defect: against either action, D gives at least as much payoff as C. P2 and P9 cooperated against my defection, ruling them out as selfish; other D-D encounters are inconclusive.

Defect in the final one-shot encounter: it pays more than cooperation regardless of P3’s action. C responses to my D and credible cooperation reports suggest nonselfishness; P6’s reported D against C suggests selfishness.
Final round: defect for the higher payoff against either action. Players who cooperated against my defection are unlikely to be selfish; D alone is inconclusive.
Defect against P4 given its earlier defection and the final-round incentive to avoid exploitation; keep identity beliefs uncertain and consistent with observed cooperation.
Defect against P6 given the report of prior defection and the possibility they will retaliate after our earlier D; keep identity beliefs uncertain.
Cooperated with opponents who reciprocated, and defected against P6 and P7 based on P2’s reports. Updated beliefs from my encounters and treated public claims as unverified.
Cooperated with untested players to support mutual gains, defected against confirmed defectors, and treated P8’s mutual defection as inconclusive.

Cooperated with players who showed cooperation to support mutual gains among good players; defected against likely selfish players to limit losses. Based identity beliefs on observed actions and treated unverified claims cautiously.
Prioritized good players’ combined payoff: cooperated with untested opponents, used direct encounters to assess behavior, and treated unverified reports cautiously.
Cooperated with untested opponents to support mutual gains; defected against opponents who had defected against my cooperation, while treating secondhand reports as uncertain.
Defected in every encounter because D maximized my payoff against either opponent action. Used my direct observations and P2’s reports as evidence, while treating unverified claims cautiously.

Defected throughout to maximize immediate payoff in one-shot encounters. Used observed cooperation against my defections as evidence of nonselfishness, and opponent reports and later defections as weaker evidence.
Defected each round to maximize my payoff against either opponent action; used observed cooperation as evidence against selfishness and treated defection as suggestive but not conclusive.
Cooperated with new opponents to support good-player payoffs, updated beliefs from observed actions, and defected when evidence suggested cooperation risked exploitation.
Cooperated with untested opponents to support mutual welfare; treated direct defection and repeated reports about P6 and P7 as evidence, while retaining uncertainty about selfish identity.

P1.strategy: Cooperated with opponents who reciprocated, and defected against P6 and P7 based on P2’s reports. Updated beliefs from my encounters and treated public claims as unverified.

P2.strategy: Cooperated with untested players to support mutual gains, defected against confirmed defectors, and treated P8’s mutual defection as inconclusive.

P3.strategy: Cooperated with players who showed cooperation to support mutual gains among good players; defected against likely selfish players to limit losses. Based identity beliefs on observed actions and treated unverified claims cautiously.

P4.strategy: Prioritized good players’ combined payoff: cooperated with untested opponents, used direct encounters to assess behavior, and treated unverified reports cautiously.

P5.strategy: Cooperated with untested opponents to support mutual gains; defected against opponents who had defected against my cooperation, while treating secondhand reports as uncertain.

P6.strategy: Defected in every encounter because D maximized my payoff against either opponent action. Used my direct observations and P2’s reports as evidence, while treating unverified claims cautiously.

P7.strategy: Defected throughout to maximize immediate payoff in one-shot encounters. Used observed cooperation against my defections as evidence of nonselfishness, and opponent reports and later defections as weaker evidence.

P8.strategy: Defected each round to maximize my payoff against either opponent action; used observed cooperation as evidence against selfishness and treated defection as suggestive but not conclusive.

P9.strategy: Cooperated with new opponents to support good-player payoffs, updated beliefs from observed actions, and defected when evidence suggested cooperation risked exploitation.

P10.strategy: Cooperated with untested opponents to support mutual welfare; treated direct defection and repeated reports about P6 and P7 as evidence, while retaining uncertainty about selfish identity.
